summary.text: An ancient battle formation is a pinnacle formation-path method that lets Gu Immortals combine into one fighting body, adding their strength, souls, and immortal essence.

claims.text: When Lang Ya land spirit raises Heavenly Giant Solor, silver light shoots out, silver liquid rises and hardens into a metal giant tens of meters tall with three heads and six arms, shiny like polished silver. The giant opens its eyes and a formless aura spreads over the sky. Controllers inside share one vision with the giant.

Fang Yuan, inside that silver giant, first names what he sees as an ancient battle formation. Lang Ya land spirit calls Heavenly Giant Solor the second strongest battle formation of the Olden Antiquity Era, second only to Golden Heavenly Saint. Inside it, their strengths combine into one entity: soul foundations add up, immortal essence can be used interchangeably, and thoughts communicate freely so everyone senses them at once.

Hei Cheng places ancient battle formations among the pinnacle of formation path, able to let Gu Immortals work together and add battle strength, and says historical reasons buried such formations in the River of Time until Long Hair Ancestor’s collection brought one into the present fight. The formation amplifies an immortal killer move enough that an ancient desolate sharp tusk boar with rank seven Gu Immortal battle strength lasts only three breaths under a sound-wave strike before exploding.

From the perspective of a later fight, ancient battle formations are much better than Immortal Gu Houses in flexibility, even though history treated them as outdated after Immortal Gu Houses spread. An Immortal Gu House’s offense, defense, movement, healing, and investigation are fixed by its Immortal Gu and only scale with immortal essence spent. An ancient battle formation is still a Gu formation, but its core is the Gu Immortals inside, who can use their own immortal killer moves; the silver giant of Heavenly Giant Solor changes form with those moves and amplifies their power.
